Alright, let me think through this year. I'm 60, been farming this same land since I was a boy, so I know what works here. My 10.9 mu isn't a lot, but with seven mouths in the household it has to pay. My wife and I do most of the farm work — two of the kids are off in the city working, and the grandkids are in school. So labor for me means mostly the two of us, plus hiring help at cotton picking time.

I split the land the way I have for years: about 7 mu in wheat-maize rotation and the remaining 3.9 mu in cotton. I know cotton prices have been soft the last few years and some of my neighbors have pulled out completely — old Liu across the road put everything into wheat-maize last season. I thought about it, but cotton still brings in cash in one lump sum in autumn, which helps with New Year expenses. I'm keeping it for now, maybe reducing further next year if prices stay bad.

**Wheat (planted last October on 7 mu):** I put down about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before planting — that's one bag per mu, easy to remember. The extension guy a few years ago told us 15 kg of nitrogen is enough, but I like to topdress about 17 kg of urea at jointing if the crop looks a bit yellow. Last year I got around 450 kg/mu, which was decent. I'll irrigate three times — the returning-green water in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if it's dry. Pumping from the well costs money, but skipping the jointing water will cost you 50 kg easily. Harvest around June 8-10, then I turn right around to plant maize.

**Maize (planted mid-June on same 7 mu):** I direct-seed Zhengdan hybrid right into the wheat stubble with the small seeder — no time to plow, the window between wheat harvest and maize planting is maybe five days. I put down 50 kg per mu of compound at planting and topdress 15 kg urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口). That gets me around 500 kg/mu usually. I only irrigate if July is dry, maybe once at tasseling. Harvest end of September.

**Cotton (planted late April on 3.9 mu):** This is the one that takes the most work. I plow and rotary-till in March, then plant Bt cotton seed mid-to-late April — bought fresh every year, about 70 yuan per mu for seed. Cotton needs less fertilizer than wheat; I do about 30 kg compound as base plus maybe 12 kg urea at the budding stage. Two irrigations: one at budding, one when the bolls are filling. Pesticide — Bt cotton takes care of bollworm but I still spray once or twice for aphids and spider mites. The hard part is picking: three rounds in September-October, my wife and I do most of it but I hire a neighbor's daughter for 5-6 days at the peak. Expecting maybe 250 kg/mu of lint if the weather holds.

**Overall thinking:** I'm not going to chase top yields — I'd rather spend a little less on inputs and keep some cash in reserve. If it's a drought year I want to still be able to pay for extra pumping. The wheat-maize is reliable; the cotton is the gamble. My total input cost comes to around 4,800 yuan for the year, most of that in fertilizer and cotton pesticide.
